```{r}
# highly colinear variables.

  "income_net_individual",

  select(age:last_col()) %>%

  setdiff(vars_exclude)

# create roll identifier
roles_df <- tibble(variable = colnames(train_df), role = NA) %>%
  mutate(role = case_when(

save_roles_df(roles_df)

roles_df %>%
```

# Missingness Analysis
## Overview of relevant cases

Analysis will be conducted for "elevated depressive scores next year" scenario, as literature outlines that interventions work best if close to potential onset. I'll visualize the relevant years in order to see before state.

```{r}
#| label: visualize relevant years
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10

train_df %>%
  select(syear, depression_phq4_binary_in_1y, all_of(vars_predictor)) %>%
  filter_relevant() %>% # see imputation_helpers for implementation, only keeps rows where depression in 1y variables are not NA
  na_heatmap_variables(highlight_borders = FALSE) -
  partial(export_return, filename = "04_na-heatmap-variables_reconstructed-filtered", width = 10, height = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: get df of only predictors for missingness testing

# make df with only the predictors. limiting to relevant rows as those are the ones i would want to impute
predictors_df <- train_df %>%
  filter_relevant() %>%
  select(all_of(vars_predictor))
```

```{r}
#| label: overall missingness

predictors_df %>%
  summarise(missing = mean(is.na(as.matrix(.))) * 100)
```

## Characteristics

```{r}
#| label: missingness characteristics

# testing mcar assumption by estimating missingness with demographic variables.

# get cols with more than 5% missingness to test
cols_test <- predictors_df %>%
  select(where(~ mean(is.na(.)) > 0.05)) %>%
  colnames()

get_lr <- function(df,
                   outcome,
                   predictors = c("age", "sex"),
                   p_sig = 0.05) {
  #' Get Likelihood ratio
  #'
  #' Get likelihood ratio test result of logit model "is specified outcome na" ~ predictors
  #'
  #' @param df : data frame
  #' @param outcome : variable to test na predictability for
  #' @param predictors : vector of columns to use as predictors in model
  #' @param p_sig : double, significance level
  #'
  #' @return likelihood-ratio

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(outcome_isna = is.na(!!sym(outcome))) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c(predictors)))

  formula <- reformulate(predictors, response = "outcome_isna")

  model <- glm(formula, data = df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  null_model <- glm(outcome_isna ~ 1,
    data = df,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )

  shorten_vars <- function(v) {
    v <- setdiff(v, "(Intercept)")
    v <- predictors[map_lgl(predictors, function(x) {
      any(grepl(x, v))
    })]
  }

  report <- tibble(
    outcome = outcome,
    lr_p = lrtest(null_model, model)$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
    mcfadden_r2 = 1 - as.numeric(logLik(model)) / as.numeric(logLik(null_model)),
    predictors = summary(model)$coefficients %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      rename(p = "Pr(>|z|)") %>%
      filter(p < p_sig) %>%
      rownames() %>%
      shorten_vars() %>%
      paste(., collapse = ", ")
  )

  return(report)
}

# Bonferroni correction
p <- 0.01 / length(cols_test)
map_dfr(cols_test, ~ get_lr(df = predictors_df, outcome = ., p_sig = p)) %>%
  rename(
    Variable = outcome,
    "Likelihood Ratio p-Value" = lr_p,
    "McFadden's pseudo-R²" = mcfadden_r2,
    "Significant Predictors" = predictors
  ) %>%
  export_return(
    "04_mar_test",
    caption = "Results of likelihood ratio tests. Compares logistic regression models predicting variable missingness with age and sex to an intercept-only baseline. Significance Level before Bonferroni Correction: 0.01.",
    label = "mar_test",
    tabular.environment = "tabularx",
    align = c("l", "R", "R", "R"),
    display = c("E", "E", "E", "f", "E"),
    digits = c(1, 1, 1, 3, 1)
  )
```


-> MCAR clearly broken, missingness in all variables with high missingness can be predicted even just with age & sex.
-> only mar strategies available

## Complete Cases

```{r}

  mutate(case_is_complete = complete.cases(.)) %>%
  summarize(n_complete = sum(case_is_complete), n_total = n()) %>%
  mutate(percent_complete = n_complete / n_total * 100)
```

```{r}

  filter_relevant() %>%
  select(syear, all_of(vars_predictor)) %>%
  group_by(syear) %>%

```

## Within-Case

```{r}
#| label: within-case missingness

within_case_missing_df <- predictors_df %>%
  mutate(
    sum = rowSums(across(everything(), is.na)),
    percent = sum / ncol(.)
  ) %>%
  select(sum, percent)

median_case_missingness <- within_case_missing_df %>%
  summarize(avg = median(percent)) %>%
  pull(avg)

print(paste0("Missingness in median case: ", median_case_missingness * 100, "%"))
```

```{r}

#| fig-width: 5
```

# Base Recipe

Basic preprocessing template to ensure equal treatment of variables.

```{r}
#| label: base recipe

recipe_base <- recipe(
  x = train_df,
  vars = roles_df$variable,
  roles = roles_df$role
) %>%
  # make weight variable recognizable as weight
  step_mutate(weight = importance_weights(weight)) %>%
  # convert logicals to factors
  step_mutate_at(all_logical(), fn = ~ factor(., levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
  # if outcome was logical, reverse order of levels
  step_mutate_at(has_role("outcome") & where(is.factor), fn = fct_rev) %>%
  # make all factors unordered
  step_unorder(all_ordered_predictors()) %>%
  # check for one-value variables (should not occur)
  step_zv(all_predictors())

recipe_base
```

# Train Imputation Techniques

Implementing 3 types of strategies: 
1. median/mode, 
2. model-based with linear model for numeric & multinomial model for factors,
3. bagged-tree


## Define recipes

```{r}
#| label: no imputation

recipe_none <- recipe_base
```

```{r}
#| label: median mean imputation

recipe_avg <- recipe_base %>%
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors())
```

For model-based we need to restrict the imputation variables a bit to avoid high missingness affecting the model.

```{r}
#| label: model-based variables

predictors_NA_df <- train_df %>%
  select(all_of(vars_predictor)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), is.na)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ scales::percent(., accuracy = 0.01))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "NA_percent"
  ) %>%
  arrange(NA_percent)

predictors_NA_df %>%
  rename(
    Variable = variable,
    "NA(%)" = NA_percent
  ) %>%
  export_return("04_na_predictors",
    caption = "Percentage of missingness present in relevant predictors before stochastic imputation.",
    label = "na_predictors"
  )
```
- > natural cutoff point at 5/10%, big gap between education_level and overtime_ever. Additionally, retaining education level important to estimate workforce & income related variables.

```{r}
#| label: model-based var selection

model_impute_vars <- predictors_NA_df %>%
  filter(NA_percent <= 5) %>%
  pull(variable)

# colnames after preprocessing steps dont match colnames from before
# due to dummy creation. dummy cols follow naming convention variableVALUE,
# so matching with startswith should be possible.
```

```{r}
#| label: model imputation

recipe_model <- recipe_base %>%
  # models require complete cases for the independent variables. thus two different procedures:
  # if im in prep ie model training, then ill drop all non-complete rows for the model predictor variables.
  # this way i only train on complete cases.
  #
  # if im instead in bake, then ill not delete anything but instead impute mean & mode for the model predictors.
  step_naomit(starts_with(model_impute_vars), skip = TRUE) %>%
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric() & starts_with(model_impute_vars)) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_factor() & starts_with(model_impute_vars)) %>%
  # now do linear imputation for numeric, custom multinomial for factors.
  step_impute_linear(all_numeric_predictors(), impute_with = starts_with(model_impute_vars)) %>%
  step_impute_multinom(all_factor_predictors(), impute_with = starts_with(model_impute_vars))
```

```{r}
#| label: bagged-tree imputation

recipe_bag <- recipe_base %>%
  step_impute_bag(all_predictors(), impute_with = imp_vars(all_predictors()))
```

```{r}
#| label: load datasets

impute_df_none <- load_imputed_df("none")
impute_df_avg <- load_imputed_df("avg")
impute_df_model <- load_imputed_df("model")
impute_df_bag <- load_imputed_df("bag")

roles_df <- load_roles_df()
```

```{r}
#| label: unify into one

cols_predictors <- roles_df %>%
  filter(role == "predictor") %>%
  pull(variable)

cols_ordered <- impute_df_none %>%
  select(all_of(cols_predictors)) %>%
  summarize(across(everything(), \(x) {
    sum(is.na(x)) / length(x) * 100
  })) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "percent"
  ) %>%
  filter(percent >= 1) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(variable, " (", floor(percent * 100) / 100, "%)")) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent)) %>%
  {
    setNames(.$label, .$variable)
  }


impute_df_all <- impute_df_none %>%
  mutate("imputation" = "none") %>%
  bind_rows(impute_df_avg %>%
    mutate("imputation" = "avg")) %>%
  bind_rows(impute_df_model %>%
    mutate("imputation" = "model")) %>%
  bind_rows(impute_df_bag %>%
    mutate("imputation" = "bag")) %>%
  select(pid, syear, imputation, all_of(cols_predictors)) %>%
  mutate(imputation = fct_inorder(imputation))

impute_df_numeric <- impute_df_all %>%
  select(pid, syear, imputation, where(is.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(pid, syear, imputation),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(cols_ordered)))


impute_df_factor <- impute_df_all %>%
  select(pid, syear, imputation, where(is.factor)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(pid, syear, imputation),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(cols_ordered)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot differences
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 75

plot_variable <- function(colname, df_numeric, df_factor) {
  # determine if we're plotting a numeric or factor variable & get data
  if (colname %in% df_numeric$variable) {
    col_numeric <- TRUE
    dat <- filter(df_numeric, variable == colname) %>%
      drop_na()
  } else {
    col_numeric <- FALSE
    dat <- filter(df_factor, variable == colname) %>%
      drop_na()
  }

  # common baseline for every plot
  plot <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = value, fill = imputation, color = imputation)) +
    facet_wrap(~imputation, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "none" = palette_qualitative[10],
        "avg" = palette_qualitative[1],
        "model" = palette_qualitative[2],
        "bag" = palette_qualitative[3]
      )
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "none" = palette_qualitative[10],
        "avg" = palette_qualitative[1],
        "model" = palette_qualitative[2],
        "bag" = palette_qualitative[3]
      )
    ) +
    guides(color = "none") +
    guides(fill = "none") +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 10,
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = NULL,
        margin = margin(b = 5)
      )
    ) +
    labs(title = cols_ordered[[colname]], x = "", y = "")

  if (col_numeric & n_distinct(dat %>% filter(imputation == "none") %>% pull(value)) > 20) {
    # col is numeric and likely continuous
    x_limits <- dat %>%
      filter(imputation == "none") %>%
      summarize(
        lower = quantile(value, 0.01),
        upper = quantile(value, 0.99),
        lower_round = floor(quantile(value, 0.01) / 5) * 5,
        upper_round = ceiling(quantile(value, 0.99) / 5) * 5,
      )

    plot <- plot +
      scale_x_continuous(
        trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(base = 10),
        breaks = {
          x <- seq(
            log(x_limits$lower_round + 1),
            log(x_limits$upper_round + 1),
            length.out = 8
          )
          x <- exp(x) - 1
          x <- sign(x) * floor(abs(x) + 0.5)
          unique(x)
        },
        labels = label_number(accuracy = 1, scale_cut = cut_short_scale())
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = c(x_limits$lower_round, x_limits$upper_round)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.2)
  } else if (col_numeric) {
    # variable is numeric & has few possible values
    plot <- plot +
      geom_histogram(
        aes(y = after_stat(density)), # only works bc of binwidth = 1, bc probability = density*width!
        binwidth = 1,
        alpha = 0.2
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(min(dat$value), max(dat$value), by = 1),
        labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())
      )
  } else {
    # variable is not numeric, is factor
    plot <- plot +
      geom_bar(
        aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = 1),
        alpha = 0.2
      ) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust = 1))
  }

  return(plot)
}


# all plots, split for appendix pages
plot_split_interval <- 5
plot_first_page <- 3 # first page should only contain 3 plots
plot_splits <- c(1, seq(plot_first_page + 1, length(cols_ordered), by = plot_split_interval))

impute_dist_plots <- map(
  names(cols_ordered),
  \(x) plot_variable(x, impute_df_numeric, impute_df_factor)
) %>%
  # remove imputation technique label from all but first plot
  imap(\(plot, i) {
    if (i %in% plot_splits) {
      plot
    } else {
      plot + theme(strip.text = element_blank())
    }
  })

# split into chunks of 5
for (img_nr in seq_along(plot_splits)) {
  i <- plot_splits[img_nr]
  if (img_nr < length(plot_splits)) {
    # not yet last plot
    end <- plot_splits[img_nr + 1] - 1
  } else {
    # last plot
    end <- length(impute_dist_plots)
  }

  wrap_plots(impute_dist_plots[i:end], ncol = 1) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Distribution of Predictor Variables before & after Imputation",
      subtitle = "Percentage indicates Missingness before Imputation"
    ) -
    partial(export_return,
      filename = paste0("04_imputation_predictors_before_after_", img_nr),
      width = 10,
      height = (end - i + 1) * 3
    )
}

# select plots only

wrap_plots(impute_dist_plots[main_text_ids], ncol = 1) +
```
